summary: Source maps become readable from the CLI: `fractal subject show <subject> --source [--node] [--revision]` shows where an agent, mission, step run or node is declared with repo@sha permalinks and helper frames; `fractal source where <path[:line]|file|GitHub URL>` lists the live subjects a file or line declares, feeds or is used by; `fractal source diff <subject> [A..B]` shows the file and canonical KDL diff between two mapped revisions and why it changed. `work claim` prints the step's SOURCE row, and step-timeout and broken-gate faults name the declaring line. New reads: GET /v1/source-maps/revisions, /v1/source-maps/where and /v1/source-maps/declaration; GET /v1/source-maps accepts step-run subjects.

replay.detail: No replay change; the new reads derive from existing source.mapped claims and their blobs at request time.

schema.detail: No SQL migration and no new claim kind. Fault and gate-failure reasons gain a trailing declaring location when the run's revision is mapped.

rules.detail: No admission or reconciliation rule changes; the declaring line is presentation only.

compatibility.detail: Additive HTTP routes and CLI subcommands. An older daemon answers the new routes with 404, which the CLI reports. Against an older daemon, step-run SOURCE lookups (which the old daemon answers as an unknown subject) show no SOURCE row instead of an error. Revisions published without a source map show no SOURCE row.

recovery.detail: Read-only feature; rolling back removes the commands and routes without touching state.
